questions.question: When stopping at an intersection, use your mirrors to:

options.text: See if drivers behind you notice you are stopping.
Look for dark clouds that may mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: See if drivers behind you notice you are stopping.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to see vehicles coming from behind. Make sure drivers see you and respond to your stop.

questions.question: Before every ride, check that:

options.text: The paint on your bike is not peeling.

questions.explanation: Do a safety check before every ride. Test your brakes to make sure the brake lights turn on.

questions.question: Service signs are what color?
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Stop quickly by pressing both brakes at the same time with controlled pressure. Do not lock the brakes.

questions.question: The best motorcycle clothing:

options.text: Should not stand out to other drivers.

questions.explanation: Proper riding clothes protect you during a crash while keeping you comfortable and visible to other drivers.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face. A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to:
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast may cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road. Slow down before entering a turn.

questions.question: Unlike other substances, alcohol:

options.text: Must be digested before entering the bloodstream.

questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested. It enters the bloodstream directly through the stomach and small intestine, reaching the brain quickly.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you most visible and keeps safe space around your bike.
You like, without thinking about other drivers.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you most visible and keeps safe space around your bike.
questions.explanation: Position yourself where other drivers can see you best and where you can keep space around your motorcycle. Change your position as traffic conditions change.

questions.question: Reflective and brightly-colored helmets and clothing:

options.text: Should only be worn at night.
Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
Do not make a motorcycle rider safer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help motorcycle riders be more visible.
questions.explanation: Wearing bright or reflective clothing helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Places you right next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you avoid hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding, wear boots or shoes that:
questions.explanation: Riding boots should be high and sturdy to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be low so they do not catch on things. Shoelaces should be tucked in so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: A rider's boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: Which colors should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, and green are the best colors for riders. These colors help other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Assume all controls are in the same place as your motorcycle.
Take it directly onto the highway.
Get familiar with it in a safe, controlled area first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get familiar with it in a safe, controlled area first.
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Learn where all the controls are before riding. Practice in a controlled area to get used to the motorcycle before riding on the road.

questions.question: Wind noise when riding:

options.text: Is easy to get used to.

questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can cause permanent hearing damage. Use ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: A good way to handle a tailgater is to:
questions.explanation: The best way to deal with a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up may make them tailgate you at a higher speed, which is even more dangerous.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you. This means:

options.text: Your fingertips barely reach the handlebars when seated.
The seat is one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet comfortably touch the ground when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet comfortably touch the ground when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you correctly if your feet comfortably touch the ground while you sit on it. Check that a motorcycle fits you before riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign tells you that a divided roadway is coming up.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, it should:

options.text: Fit loosely and flap in the wind.
Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
Not be made of leather or sturdy material.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants made of leather or sturdy material. They should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but loose enough to let you move freely.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, what should matter most?
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles traveling below 25 mph, such as farm equipment, construction vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: When choosing a jacket for protection, a motorcycle rider should pick one that is:

options.text: Made of leather or synthetic materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Made of leather or synthetic materials.
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. Choose a jacket that covers your arms completely and fits snugly but allows you to move freely. Leather or sturdy synthetic materials with body armor offer the best protection.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection in a crash?
questions.explanation: Leather or sturdy synthetic materials provide the best crash protection. Riders should wear long pants and jackets while riding.
